newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short depos soft, mkt concerned about taxes.
newsitem.headline: Greek short depos soft, mkt concerned about taxes.

text.p: Greek short-term depos were easier and forex forwards were fluctuating narrowly in early unexciting dealing while traders were awaiting to hear the government's final decision on the taxation of T-bills and FRNs.

"Depos are softer in short periods on improved liquidity," said a trader at a state bank. "Some T-bill expiries will boost liquidity but it remains to be seen what banks that have made use of the central bank's facility will do."

Commercial banks are allowed to withdraw 10 percent of the portion of their required reserves at the central bank that earn no interest to cope with temporary liquidity shortages but they should keep their average reserves steady for the period ending November 10.
Reserve requirements stand at 12 percent and half of it earns no interest with the rest earning a rate of 12.5 percent.

Sales of T-bills last Thursday turned out exceptionally strong, with traders saying fixed income investors were expecting the government to decide in favour of taxing interest earned on state debt paper in the near future.
About 470 billion drachmas of book-entry T-bills were sold on Thursday.
Traders said they were concerned about the impact of taxes on interest earned from state securities as heralded in the local press but they were awaiting the government's final decision on the issue.
The mark was quoted at 157.36/41 drachmas from Friday's 157.025 fix, the dollar at 238.10/15 drachmas from 238.600 and the Ecu at 301.79/89 from 301.620 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma has firmed in early trade. Market concern about the taxation of T-bills and FRNs could be the reason," said a forex trader.
